item_7.notes:
[chunk 1/1] Filing: Alphabet (GOOGL) 10-K, FY2023, Item 7 MD&A.

KEY EXTRACTIONS:

1. CAPEX & PURCHASE OBLIGATIONS: FY2023 capex was $32.3B (up from $31.5B in 2022), with explicit forward guidance to increase further for AI infrastructure. Separately, $45.9B in non-cancellable purchase commitments as of Dec 31, 2023 ($31.6B short-term), primarily for technical infrastructure — a material CAPEX_ROI_GAP signal given no matched contracted revenue is disclosed.

2. COST OPACITY — DEPRECIATION LIFE CHANGE: In Jan 2023, Alphabet extended server and network equipment useful lives to 6 years, reducing depreciation by $3.9B in FY2023. This is a Severity 3 COST_OPACITY signal — it materially flattered operating income (Google Cloud turned profitable in 2023, partly aided by this change) and distorts YoY comparability.

3. HIDDEN LEVERAGE — OFF-BALANCE-SHEET LEASES: $3.957B in signed-but-not-yet-commenced leases (not on balance sheet), commencing 2024–2026, with terms up to 25 years. Total on-balance-sheet operating lease obligations are $17.7B at 8-year weighted avg term.

4. NON-MARKETABLE EQUITY: The MD&A references non-marketable equity securities measured under the "measurement alternative" with unobservable inputs, including performance fee compensation tied to realized returns. The specific investee roster is not named in this Item 7 section — it would appear in Note 3/Note 8 of Item 8, not extracted here per source text scope.

5. NO NAMED AI LAB COUNTERPARTIES: This Item 7 excerpt does not name specific AI lab investments (e.g., Anthropic) or cloud compute customers. Those would appear in Item 1A Risk Factors or financial statement notes. No fabricated counterparties have been added.

6. REGULATORY: EC fines totaling ~$9.5B equivalent across 2017–2019 decisions are accrued (bank guarantees in lieu of cash), plus active DOJ antitrust litigation — Severity 3 legal risk flagged.

financial_statements_and_notes.notes:
[chunk 1/3] FILING SECTION COVERAGE: This section covers the auditor reports, consolidated financial statements (balance sheets, income statements, cash flows, stockholders' equity), and the beginning of the Notes to Financial Statements (Notes 1–2 and the opening of Note 3). Key observations:

1. COST_OPACITY (Severity 3): Alphabet extended server useful lives from 4→6 years and network equipment from 5→6 years in January 2023, reducing FY2023 depreciation by $3.9B and boosting net income by $3.0B ($0.24/share). This is a material accounting estimate change that inflates reported profitability. With $134B of PP&E on balance sheet, the longer depreciation schedule also masks true asset aging and replacement cadence risk.

2. CIRCULARITY / REVENUE_ROUNDTRIP (Severity 3): Note 1 explicitly discloses that Alphabet holds "debt and equity investments in companies with which we also entered into commercial arrangements at or near the same time," requiring judgment on whether components should be separate transactions and noting that investment impairment could reduce performance obligations. This is a textbook revenue-roundtrip / circularity signal. No specific counterparties are named in this section — they would appear in Note 3 (Financial Instruments) or Note 8 (non-marketable securities), which are not included in this excerpt.

3. EXECUTION_RISK (Severity 2): $74.1B Google Cloud revenue backlog as of Dec 31 2023, with only ~half expected within 24 months. Recognition is contingent on Alphabet's delivery capability and customer utilization, creating substantial execution risk given the scale of cloud infrastructure investment underway.

4. CAPEX: $32.25B in PP&E purchases in FY2023 (vs $31.5B in FY2022), with no named counterparty commitments disclosed in this section. Total non-marketable securities balance of $31.0B (up from $30.5B) suggests continued private-company investment activity.

5. No SPV/off-balance-sheet entities, named AI lab investments, or specific counterparty capex commitments were disclosed in this section.
